display_name: Singapore retrenchment benefit norm and Workfare Income Supplement -- as published
citation: Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment (updated 20 January 2023), Annex C part II, as published by the Ministry of Manpower and the Tripartite Alliance; Workfare Income Supplement Scheme, as published by the Central Provident Fund Board
authority: Ministry of Manpower, Singapore (with NTUC and SNEF as tripartite partners); Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management; Central Provident Fund Board

source.note: ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY AS PUBLISHED, NOT LAW. The retrenchment benefit norm is a tripartite guideline (MOM, NTUC, SNEF); MOM's own FAQ says retrenchment benefit is not mandated by law, and the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management says it is not compulsory under the Employment Act. The Advisory refers to the Employment Act only for the mandatory retrenchment notification; whatever the Employment Act itself provides is left to subjects/sg/employment-act-1968. The Workfare Income Supplement is a Government scheme administered by the CPF Board; its figures are set and changed by announcement, not by amending an Act, and the employee's share is paid partly into CPF accounts (the Central Provident Fund Act's own tests are left to subjects/sg/central-provident-fund-act-1953). Each figure in the encoding carries the date of the page it came from. Pages read on 12 October 2026; nothing was deposited.
